tier_reason: The README states Pyston full is 'roughly 30% faster than CPython on web serving macrobenchmarks' and pyston-lite 'roughly 10% faster on macrobenchmarks', with no CPU, compiler flags, CPython version or run counts; the benchmark code (pyston/python-macrobenchmarks submodule, run via pyperformance 'pyston_standard') is public but no result table or methodology accompanies the numbers, so first-party tier C.

corrections.license: Python-2.0 (CPython license stack: PSF License Version 2 with BeOpen, CNRI and CWI agreements; root LICENSE is CPython's)
corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers ('roughly 30%' full, 'roughly 10%' lite) with no CPU, flags, CPython version or run counts; benchmark suite is public (pyston/python-macrobenchmarks, pyperformance manifest 'pyston_standard') but no result table is published in the repo. Baseline is CPython of the 3.7-3.10 era; newer CPython releases are not compared, and PyPy is not compared. Repository description says '(No longer maintained)'; the last code change was the Feb 28, 2023 merge of PR #301 and the Aug 12, 2024 commits only touch issue templates. Licence: the only LICENSE file is CPython's (PSF License Version 2 stack); no Apache-2.0 text was found (no pyston/ or pyston_lite LICENSE, JIT sources such as Python/aot_ceval_jit.c carry no header, PyPI pyston-lite lists no licence); the Apache-2.0 claim likely comes from the separate Pyston v1 repo. Pyston-full is API- but not ABI-compatible with CPython, so C extensions must be recompiled.

notes: README numbers match the record. Licence corrected from Apache-2.0 to the CPython Python-2.0/PSF-2.0 licence stack (OSI-approved, so usability stays copyable). maintenance_status kept 'abandoned' because the authors declare it no longer maintained, although the last commit (2024-08-12) is only about 2 years old; shortcomings: first-party vague percentages, no methodology, CPython-3.8-era baseline, unmaintained.

tier_reason: The README mermaid quadrant chart gives exactly the normalized compile/execution scores in the record for WARP, V8 Liftoff/TurboFan and SpiderMonkey Baseline/Ion; the harness (scripts/benchmark/run_bench.py, util/d8_harness.js, util/sm_harness.js) and build flags are public, but no CPU model, compiler or engine versions are stated, the normalization to 0-1 is undocumented, and the benchmark input repo (Schleifner/open-wasm-compiler-benchmark) returns 404, so first-party tier C.

corrections.workload: Normalized compilation speed and execution speed of WebAssembly modules from the open-wasm-compiler-benchmark repo (github.com/Schleifner/open-wasm-compiler-benchmark, which returns 404 as of 2026-10-06, so the inputs are not public), WARP's vb_bench versus V8 d8 (Liftoff, TurboFan) and SpiderMonkey js shell (Baseline, Ion) and native clang builds, timed by scripts/benchmark/run_bench.py.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Benchmark guide (scripts/benchmark/Readme.md): vb_bench built with clang/clang++, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, -DINTERRUPTION_REQUEST=0 -DEAGER_ALLOCATION=1, VB_ENABLE_DEV_FEATURE=OFF; V8 d8 built with tools/dev/gm.py x64.release and run with --no-wasm-lazy-compilation --liftoff or --no-liftoff --single-threaded; SpiderMonkey built with an optimized mozconfig and run with --wasm-compiler=baseline or ion --cpu-count=1. Compiler, V8 and SpiderMonkey versions not stated.
corrections.caveats: Result is a normalized unitless quadrant chart; run_bench.py prints wall-clock means and a score of 10000/geomean, but how the 0-1 chart values were derived is not documented, and native clang's compile score is a placeholder 0.5 ('comp. speed N/A'). CPU model and tool versions are not stated. Benchmark inputs (Schleifner/open-wasm-compiler-benchmark) are not publicly reachable (404). Harness flaws: the compilation benchmark times the whole process with /usr/bin/time -p (10 ms resolution), so d8 and SpiderMonkey js-shell startup and JS harness load are charged to their compile time while WARP runs as a small native binary, which favours WARP; default is a single run per module (-n 1); the 'V8 Liftoff' runs do not pass --no-wasm-tier-up, so hot code may tier up to TurboFan. WARP's execution score (0.8172) is below V8 TurboFan (0.8505) and native clang (0.873) and about equal to SpiderMonkey Ion (0.8163); its win is compile speed at near-optimizing-tier execution speed, and clearly over the single-pass baselines Liftoff (0.4275) and SpiderMonkey Baseline (0.3456). Backing paper (Scheidl, Valent-Blocks, iCCECE 2020) was not opened (IEEE and ResearchGate blocked); a search snippet only says WebAssembly overhead on embedded targets fell from 87% to 21%.

notes: Chart numbers match the record exactly; metadata confirmed (Apache-2.0, 26 stars, last commit 2026-10-03 'Fix CI apt install (#865)', active, BMW AG copyright on harness files). Main shortcomings: undocumented normalization, no CPU or versions, benchmark inputs repo 404, whole-process wall-clock timing charges JS-engine startup to V8/SpiderMonkey compile times.
